title: Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation — from gene discovery to therapeutic strategies
title_zh: 伴脑铁沉着的神经退行性疾病——从基因发现到治疗策略
abstract: Precision therapeutics are emerging for various neurological disorders, most notably single-gene disorders. Development of breakthrough treatments typically requires insight into the earliest pathogenic changes, which enables intervention before irreversible damage to cell function has occurred. At the extreme, presymptomatic gene therapy could subvert entire disease processes. The neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (NBIA) disorders exemplify progress from Mendelian disease gene discovery to the era of precision neurotherapeutics. These disorders highlight the opportunities and challenges in developing precision therapeutics for single-gene neurological disorders. In this Review, we discuss the most common NBIA disorders to highlight how the study of genetic disorders can provide insight into basic neuroscience and the brain’s regional vulnerability. We discuss in detail the biology of pantothenate kinase-associated neurodegeneration (PKAN), which underscores the complex and poorly understood biochemistry of this apparently simple inborn error of vitamin metabolism, and also forges a path for novel interventions. The progress in understanding of and therapeutic development for PKAN exemplifies the beginning of a rise in breakthrough therapies for genetic neurological disorders. The neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (NBIA) disorders exemplify progress from Mendelian disease gene discovery to the era of precision neurotherapeutics. In this Review, Hayflick and Sibon discuss the most common NBIA disorders to highlight how the study of genetic disorders can provide insight into basic neuroscience and the brain’s regional vulnerability.
